questions.topic_aspect: Combining multiple circle theorems (angle at centre, isosceles triangles from radii)

questions.topic_aspect: Show that — combining cyclic quadrilateral and tangent (alternate segment) properties
questions.mark_scheme:
M1: Use cyclic quadrilateral theorem (opposite angles sum to 180°) to find angle DAB = 180 − 118 = 62°, with theorem named.
M1: Use alternate segment theorem (tangent-chord angle = angle in alternate segment) to identify angle ADF = angle DAB (or equivalent chain identifying angle ADF = angle ABC's alternate angle), naming theorem.
M1: Correct construction of angle chain: angle ADC = angle ADF + angle FDC or use angle ADC = 180° − angle ADF's supplementary relation via straight line EDF and cyclic quad property to reach 118°, with full reasoning shown (not just numbers).
A1: Correct conclusion angle ADC = 118° with all theorem names stated explicitly (cyclic quadrilateral, alternate segment theorem, angles on a straight line) forming a logical chain.
questions.misconception_targeted: Not structuring a logical chain of reasoning with theorem names when proving a result rather than just calculating a number
